issues_outside_coverage: Unreimbursed employee business expenses (Schedule A, Form 2106/2106-EZ) of $26,969 (2015) and $31,372 (2016) disallowed in full: vehicle, parking/tolls, travel, meals and entertainment (sec. 274(d) strict substantiation), business expenses and union dues (no basis for Cohan estimate), clothing/laundry/tools (no showing reimbursement unavailable), cellular phone (no basis for estimate; reimbursable)

Concessions: petitioner conceded $8,888 of additional 2015 mortgage interest and points; respondent conceded $727 real estate taxes and $1,802 points for 2015 and that $2,234 of 2016 State refunds is not income
Itemized deductions vs. standard deduction under married filing separate status (computational)
decisive_judgment_findings: Petitioner was legally married under California law throughout 2015 and 2016 and offered no evidence of a decree of divorce or separate maintenance (spouse filed as head of household)
Petitioner kept no contemporaneous records of business purpose, mileage logs, or proof that expenses were not reimbursable under the employer's policy
Credible testimony that protective clothing and tools were required, but no showing that reimbursement was sought and denied
Decision under Rule 155 with no final deficiency figures stated; no deficiency value recorded (notice deficiencies were $6,840 for 2015 and $6,942 for 2016, adjusted by concessions)
